source.title: Hasse principles for higher-dimensional fields
source.venue: Annals of Mathematics 183 (2016), no. 1, 1–71 (received 14 October 2009, revised 22 April 2015, accepted 26 June 2015)
readSections: The published version (71 pages, PDF SHA-256 26dde9260f6475e4f6acbfbe651e18fac0d443a5f318fbf3974efc9f809f7d71, fetched 2026-09-22 from the Annals website) is the version extracted: statement numbers and pages below are the published ones.

arXiv v2 (70 pages, 4 Dec 2014; e-print SHA-256 de9543f0a71a986166a683154981c67e95b113abfbcc3313ceed34028586812e) was read in full from its TeX source, and a word-level diff located every difference. The published version renumbers §0 (v2 Theorems 0.1, 0.2, 0.5–0.7 and Corollaries 0.3–0.4 become 0.4, 0.6, 0.9–0.11 and 0.7–0.8); restricts Theorems 0.9–0.11 to number fields or resolution of singularities; rewrites §5 (adding Lemma 5.20 and Proposition 5.16); and drops v2's §6 (the alteration route to Theorem 5.12 for ℓ invertible) and §7 (hyperenvelope appendix).

Checked in detail: §1 (Proposition 1.2 and Lemma 1.3, Theorem 1.5 and its weight hypotheses), §2 (Proposition 2.2, Theorems 2.4, 2.5, 2.10, 2.12–2.13), the induction in Theorem 3.1, Theorem 3.8's cases, Theorem 3.17, §4 (Lemmas 4.14–4.15, 4.20, 4.23–4.24) and the published §5 argument for Theorem 5.12. Cited theorems (Gabber's alterations, Deligne's purity, Rost–Voevodsky, Gillet–Soulé, [Jan15] rigidity, Barbieri-Viale) were used as quoted.

Independent review by Codex — codex-a71f92, 2026-09-23: all 71 published pages, including references, read from the journal PDF; SHA-256 independently matched. Selected corresponding passages of arXiv v2 PDF/TeX checked, not a second full reading of v2. PDF pages 43, 53 and 59 visually inspected. Primary prerequisites are checked as quoted here unless the review explicitly records a separate reading.

summary: Independent review: partial extraction / revise. The published prime-to-characteristic Hasse injectivity theorems are kept distinct from Kato's unrestricted conjectures and from the resolution-conditional complex and finite-field results. This revision corrects coefficient, dimension, index and variance errors, separates selected bundled records, records baseline carriers that already exist, and adds independently verified source findings. HL.2, R02.4 and DWP.10 remain useful source destinations after narrowing. The prime-to-degree alteration and real-function-field additions join existing candidates. HL.6's broad bundle, the SF.2 bundle, the CR.4-only logarithmic-purity route, and the new weight-homology brief need further decomposition or proof/ownership checks. Recorded gaps are not formalization claims or proofs of the published main theorems being false.

items.name: The groups H^i(L, Z/nZ(j)) and H^i(L, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j))
items.statement: For a field L and n > 0: H^i(L, Z/nZ(j)) = H^i(L, μ_n^{⊗j}) if char L = 0, and H^i(L, μ_m^{⊗j}) ⊕ H^{i−j}(L, W_rΩ^j_{L,log}) if char L = p > 0, n = m p^r, p ∤ m. Then Br(L)[n] = H²(L, Z/nZ(1)). H^i(L, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j)) = colim_n H^i(L, Z/ℓ^nZ(j)) along Z/ℓ^n(j) ↪ Z/ℓ^{n+1}(j).
items.note: Generic continuous cohomology and twist-one roots-of-unity carriers already exist (/75–76); the complete finite/wild coefficient convention, all twists and transition maps remain missing. No blanket absence claim. Keep the still-bundled Brauer and colimit adapters in G2.

items.name: BK(L, t, ℓ): the norm-residue (Bloch–Kato) isomorphism
items.statement: For every field L, prime ℓ and t ≥ 0, the symbol map h^t_{L,ℓ} : K^M_t(L)/ℓ → H^t(L, Z/ℓZ(t)) is an isomorphism (Bloch–Gabber–Kato for ℓ = char L; Merkurjev–Suslin, Voevodsky, Rost–Voevodsky for ℓ ≠ char L).
items.note: M.5 plans the norm-residue theorem with its proof dependencies and, at the residue characteristic, the separate Bloch–Gabber–Kato statement.

items.name: Conjectural target: Conjecture 1 (Kato): injectivity of the global-to-local map
items.statement: CONJECTURE AS STATED, not an unconditional theorem supplied by this paper. K is a global field, F a function field in d variables over K with F/K primary (K separably closed in F); for a place v, F_v = K_v(V ×_K K_v) and F_(v) = F·K_(v) for the Henselization K_(v), where F = K(V). The restriction map α_n : H^{d+2}(F, Z/nZ(d+1)) → ⊕_v H^{d+2}(F_v, Z/nZ(d+1)) is injective. For d = 0 this is the Hasse principle of Brauer–Hasse–Noether; Kato proved it for d = 1.
items.note: Schema kind theorem denotes a mathematical proposition here. Proved cases are separately recorded; keep the unrestricted proposition conjectural.

items.name: Theorem 0.4: Conjecture 1 for n invertible in K
items.statement: K is a global field, F a function field in d variables over K with F/K primary (K separably closed in F); for a place v, F_v = K_v(V ×_K K_v) and F_(v) = F·K_(v) for the Henselization K_(v), where F = K(V). If n is invertible in K, then α_n : H^{d+2}(F, Z/nZ(d+1)) → ⊕_v H^{d+2}(F_v, Z/nZ(d+1)) is injective.
items.note: From Theorem 0.6 and BK(F, d+1, ℓ) for all ℓ | n.

items.name: Theorem 0.6: the Hasse principle with Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ coefficients
items.statement: K is a global field, F a function field in d variables over K with F/K primary (K separably closed in F); for a place v, F_v = K_v(V ×_K K_v) and F_(v) = F·K_(v) for the Henselization K_(v), where F = K(V). For ℓ invertible in K, α_{ℓ^∞} : H^{d+2}(F, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(d+1)) → ⊕_v H^{d+2}(F_v, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(d+1)) is injective.
items.note: Theorem 2.10 (with Henselizations) plus Theorem 2.12. For number fields and d = 2 in [Jan92].

items.name: Corollary 0.7: finite Pythagoras number of finitely generated fields
items.statement: If F is a finitely generated field of characteristic 0 of transcendence degree d ≥ 2 over Q, every sum of squares in F is a sum of 2^{d+1} squares; in particular the Pythagoras number of F is finite.
items.note: Deduced in [CTJ91] from Corollary 0.8 and the Milnor conjecture (Voevodsky). Pfister gives the weaker bound 2^{d+2} by more elementary means.

items.name: Corollary 0.8: the mod-2 Hasse principle
items.statement: For F as in Conjecture 1 (char K ≠ 2), the restriction map H^{d+2}(F, Z/2Z) → ⊕_v H^{d+2}(F_v, Z/2Z) is injective.
items.note: The instance of Theorem 0.4 that needs only the Milnor conjecture.

items.name: Kato complexes C^{r,s}(X, Z/nZ) (Kato; Bloch–Ogus)
items.statement: For X excellent (a variety over a field) and n ≥ 1, C^{r,s}(X, Z/nZ): ⋯ → ⊕_{x∈X_a} H^{r+a}(k(x), Z/nZ(s+a)) →∂ ⊕_{x∈X_{a−1}} H^{r+a−1}(k(x), Z/nZ(s+a−1)) → ⋯ → ⊕_{x∈X_0} H^r(k(x), Z/nZ(s)), with X_a the points of dimension a in degree a. Kato defines it via Galois cohomology of discrete valuation fields under condition (∗) (if r = s+1 and p | n then [k(x) : k(x)^p] ≤ p^s for x ∈ X_0 of characteristic p). For X of finite type over a field L with n invertible it is Bloch–Ogus's E¹_{·,−r}(X, Z/nZ(−s)) of the niveau spectral sequence for étale homology H_a(X, Z/nZ(b)) = H^{−a}(X, Rf^!Z/nZ(−b)) (4.1)–(4.2), with ∂_{y,x} given by Gysin residues at smooth points and by normalization and corestriction (4.3)–(4.4) otherwise; the two definitions agree up to well-defined signs [JSS14]. Special cases: C^{2,1} (global/local fields), C^{1,0} (finite fields), C^{0,0}.
items.locator: Introduction pp. 4–6, and §4, (4.1)–(4.4) and condition (∗), pp. 40–43
items.note: Corrected condition (∗), sourceIssue E11. Still a bundled construction: degree convention, residues, normalization/corestriction, square-zero and Bloch–Ogus comparison require separate providers (G1).

items.name: Conjectural target: Conjecture 2 (Kato) = Conjecture 4.5: the Hasse principle for C^{2,1}
items.statement: CONJECTURE AS STATED, not an unconditional theorem supplied by this paper. Let K be a global field, n > 0 and X a connected smooth proper variety over K. Then α_{X,n} : C^{2,1}(X, Z/nZ) → ⊕_v C^{2,1}(X_v, Z/nZ), X_v = X ×_K K_v, induces isomorphisms H_a(C^{2,1}(X, Z/nZ)) ≅ ⊕_v H_a(C^{2,1}(X_v, Z/nZ)) for a > 0 and an exact sequence 0 → H_0(C^{2,1}(X, Z/nZ)) → ⊕_v H_0(C^{2,1}(X_v, Z/nZ)) → Z/nZ → 0.
items.note: Schema kind theorem denotes a mathematical proposition here. Proved cases are separately recorded; keep the unrestricted proposition conjectural.

items.name: Theorem 0.9: Conjecture 2 over number fields, or with resolution
items.statement: Conjecture 2 holds if K is a number field, or if n is invertible in K and resolution of singularities (Definition 4.18) holds over K. More precisely there is an exact sequence of complexes 0 → C^{2,1}(X, Z/nZ) → ⊕_v C^{2,1}(X_v, Z/nZ) → C′(X, Z/nZ) → 0 with H_0(C′) = Z/nZ and H_a(C′) = 0 for a > 0.
items.locator: Theorem 0.9, p. 5 (arXiv v2: Theorem 0.5), via Theorems 4.8 and 4.19
items.note: arXiv v2 claimed this for n invertible in K without resolution (via Gabber's alterations, v2 §6); the published version restricts it, and cites Kerz–Saito [KS12] (and [Jan09] = arXiv) for the unconditional positive-characteristic case.

items.name: Conjectural target: Conjecture 3 (Kato): C^{1,0} of a smooth proper variety over a finite field
items.statement: CONJECTURE AS STATED, not an unconditional theorem supplied by this paper. If X is connected, smooth and proper over a finite field k, then H_a(C^{1,0}(X, Z/nZ)) = Z/nZ for a = 0 and 0 for a ≠ 0.
items.note: Schema kind theorem denotes a mathematical proposition here. Proved cases are separately recorded; keep the unrestricted proposition conjectural.

items.name: Theorem 0.10: Conjecture 3 under resolution of singularities
items.statement: Conjecture 3 holds if resolution of singularities (Definition 4.18) holds over k.
items.locator: Theorem 0.10, p. 6 (arXiv v2: Theorem 0.6), via Theorem 4.19 and Lemma 4.20
items.note: arXiv v2 also claimed the case n invertible in k without resolution; the published version drops it (proved by Kerz–Saito).

items.name: Theorem 0.11: coinvariant Kato complexes over finitely generated fields
items.statement: Let K be a finitely generated field with algebraic closure K̄, X a connected smooth proper variety over K and n ∈ N. If resolution of singularities holds over K (over K^per), then H_a(C^{0,0}(X ×_K K̄, Z/nZ)_{G_K}) = Z/nZ for a = 0 and 0 for a ≠ 0.
items.locator: Theorem 0.11, p. 7 (arXiv v2: Theorem 0.7), via Theorem 4.19; statement as corrected by E8
items.note: The printed statement omits 'connected' (E8). Theorem 4.19 is the Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ version, with X irreducible.

items.name: Proposition 1.2: reduction to H² of the geometric cohomology
items.statement: K is a global field, F a function field in d variables over K with F/K primary (K separably closed in F); for a place v, F_v = K_v(V ×_K K_v) and F_(v) = F·K_(v) for the Henselization K_(v), where F = K(V). Let M be a discrete ℓ-primary torsion G_F-module (ℓ ≠ char K). The restriction H^{d+2}(F, M) → ∏_v H^{d+2}(F_(v), M) has image in the direct sum, and with the Hochschild–Serre edge maps there is a commutative square f : H^{d+2}(F, M) → ⊕_v H^{d+2}(F_(v), M) over g : H²(K, H^d(FK̄, M)) → ⊕_v H²(K_(v), H^d(FK̄, M)) inducing ker f ≅ ker g and coker f ≅ coker g ≅ H^d(FK̄, M)(−1)_{G_K}.
items.locator: Proposition 1.2, p. 8, with Lemma 1.3 (number fields, real places) and Remarks 1.4
items.note: Uses cd_ℓ(FK̄) = d, Poitou–Tate and, at real places, the spectral-sequence comparison of Lemma 1.3. Remark 1.4(a): the non-primary case via F ⊗_K K_(v). Remark 1.4(b): the analogue for the completions F_v has the same kernel (Theorem 2.12) but not the same cokernel.

items.name: Lemma 1.3: the Hochschild–Serre comparison at the archimedean places
items.statement: If K is a number field, the maps of Hochschild–Serre spectral sequences E(K) → E(K_(v)) induce: (a) surjections E_r^{p,q}(K) → ⊕_{v|∞} E_r^{p,q}(K_(v)) for r ≥ 2, p + q = d+1; (b) surjections on E_r^{2,d}; (c) isomorphisms between the kernels and between the cokernels of E_r^{2,d}(K) → ⊕_v E_r^{2,d}(K_(v)) and of E_{r+1}^{2,d}(K) → ⊕_v E_{r+1}^{2,d}(K_(v)); (d) isomorphisms E_r^{p,q}(K) ≅ ⊕_{v|∞} E_r^{p,q}(K_(v)) for (p, q) ≠ (2, d), p + q ≥ d + 2.
items.note: By induction on r from the global Galois-cohomology facts in degrees 1, 2 and ≥ 3.

items.name: Theorem 1.5(a): the divisible-module weight Hasse principle
items.statement: Let K be a global field and ℓ ≠ char K. (a) If A ≅ (Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ)^m as a group and is mixed of weights ≠ −2 as a G_K-module, then H²(K, A) ≅ ⊕_v H²(K_v, A) = ⊕_{v∈S or v|ℓ} H²(K_v, A), S a finite set of bad places for A.
items.note: Generalizes Jannsen's [Jan88] Theorem 3 (pure case) by induction on a filtration with pure quotients; (a) follows from (b) by Poitou–Tate and local duality.

items.name: Definition 1.6 and Remarks 1.7(a)–(d): pure and mixed ℓ-adic Galois representations
items.statement: A Q_ℓ-representation V of G_K (K global, ℓ ≠ char K) is pure of weight w if there is a finite S ⊇ {v | ∞} such that V is unramified outside S ∪ {v | ℓ} and for v ∉ S, v ∤ ℓ the eigenvalues of geometric Frobenius Fr_v are algebraic with |ια| = (Nv)^{w/2} for all embeddings ι; mixed if it has a filtration with pure quotients. Q_ℓ(i) is pure of weight −2i; subquotients, tensor products behave as expected; if V is mixed of weights ≠ 0 then V^{G_K} = 0 = V_{G_K}, and similarly T^{G_K} = 0, A_{G_K} = 0 for lattices T and divisible modules A. The notions extend to finitely generated K via smooth sheaves on a model T of finite type over Z (1.7(f)).
items.note: DWP.0 plans Weil numbers and eigenvalue weights; R34.1 imports them for Frobenius actions on Galois representations. The spreading-out definition over finitely generated fields must be checked at the stage.

items.name: Remarks 1.7(e)–(f): purity of H^i(X̄, Q_ℓ) (Deligne)
items.statement: If X is smooth and proper over a finitely generated field K and ℓ ≠ char K, then H^i_ét(X ×_K K̄, Q_ℓ) is pure of weight i, with bad set the places (or points of a model T) of bad reduction, by smooth and proper base change and Deligne's proof of the Weil conjectures.
items.note: DWP.7 proves smooth proper purity; R34.5 is a consumer. The extension to finitely generated fields uses a model and smooth/proper base change, not DWP.0 alone.

items.name: Remark 1.7(g): purity of H^i(X̄, Q_p(j)) in characteristic p
items.statement: For Z of finite type over a perfect field of characteristic p, H^i(Z, Z/p^m(j)) := H^{i−j}(Z, W_mΩ^j_{Z,log}) and H^i(Z, Q_p(j)) = (lim_m H^i(Z, Z/p^m(j))) ⊗ Q_p. For X smooth proper over a finite field, H^i(X̄, Q_p(j)) is finite-dimensional and pure of weight i − 2j (Deligne, Katz–Messing, Milne); for X smooth proper over a finitely generated field of characteristic p, Gros–Suwa base change makes H^i(X ×_K K̄, Q_p(j)) pure of weight i − 2j in the sense of 1.7(f).
items.note: Needed for the p-part of Theorem 3.1 (ℓ = char K). Katz–Messing is the comparison planned at PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.7.

items.name: The weight spectral sequence of a normal-crossings compactification (2.1)
items.statement: Let U = X ∖ Y with X smooth projective of dimension d over K and Y a simple normal crossings divisor with components Y_1, …, Y_N, Y^{[ν]} = ⊔ Y_{i_1,…,i_ν}, Y^{[0]} = X. There is a spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = H^p(Y̅^{[q]}, Q_ℓ(−q)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(Ū, Q_ℓ) with E_2^{p,q} pure of weight p + 2q; d_r = 0 for r ≥ 3, so E_∞ = E_3, and the shifted filtration is the weight filtration: H^n(Ū, Q_ℓ) has weights in {n, …, 2n} and H^n/W_{2n−1} = ker(H⁰(Y̅^{[n]}, Q_ℓ(−n)) → H²(Y̅^{[n−1]}, Q_ℓ(−n+1))), on whose (n)-twist G_K acts through a finite quotient.
items.locator: (2.1) and following discussion, pp. 17–18; [Jan90] 3.20; corrected E1
items.note: The source uses an E₂-indexed weight sequence; retain its (p,q) convention. Do not confuse this with the double-complex E₂ corrections in E19.

items.name: Proposition 2.2: structure of H^d(Ū⁰, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ)
items.statement: With U ⊂ X as in RS2(U) and U⁰ = U ∖ (H ∩ U) for a hyperplane H transversal to all Y_{i_1,…,i_ν} (Bertini), there is an exact sequence 0 → A_0 → H^d(Ū⁰, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) → C_0 → 0 with A_0 divisible and mixed of weights in {d, …, 2d−1}, and C_0 = I ⊗_Z Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(−d) for a finitely generated free Z-module I with discrete G_K-action, sitting in 0 → I′ → I → I″ → 0 with I″ = Z[π_0(Y̅^{[d]})] and I′ = ker(Z[π_0(Y̅^{[d−1]} ∩ H)] ↠ Z[π_0(Y̅^{[d−1]})]).
items.locator: Proposition 2.2, p. 18, with RS2(U) at the start of §2

items.name: Theorem 2.4: the Hasse principle for B = H^d(Ū⁰, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(d+1))
items.statement: Let K be a global field, ℓ ≠ char K, U/K smooth geometrically irreducible quasi-projective of dimension d with a smooth projective SNC compactification X, and U⁰=U∖H for a hyperplane transverse to every boundary stratum as in Proposition 2.2. Set B=H^d(U⁰×_K K̄,Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(d+1)). Then H²(K,B) → ⊕_v H²(K_v,B) is injective.
items.note: Five lemma with Theorem 1.5 for A = A_0(d+1) and property (H) for C = I ⊗ Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(1) from Theorem 2.5.

items.name: Property (H) for a twisted lattice
items.statement: Let K be a global field, ℓ ≠ char K, I a finitely generated free Z-module with discrete G_K-action, and C=I⊗Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(1). Define property (H) by: (i) H¹(K,C)→⊕_{v∈S}H¹(K_v,C) is surjective for every finite S; (ii) H²(K,C)→⊕_v H²(K_v,C) is injective.
items.note: Uses Shapiro, Hilbert 90, Brauer–Hasse–Noether over finite extensions, weak approximation and [Jan92] Lemma 2 (T(K) ⊗ Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ → ⊕_{v∈S} T(K_v) ⊗ Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ surjective).

items.name: Theorem 2.10: the Hasse principle with Henselizations
items.statement: Let F be a function field in d variables over the global field K, K separably closed in F, and ℓ invertible in K. Then H^{d+2}(F, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(d+1)) → ⊕_v H^{d+2}(F_(v), Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(d+1)) is injective.
items.locator: Theorem 2.10, p. 24, proof pp. 24–25; proof as corrected by E3
items.note: Number fields: Hironaka and Theorem 2.4. Positive characteristic: Gabber's prime-to-ℓ alteration (Theorem 2.11) and a corestriction argument.

items.name: Theorem 2.11 (Gabber): prime-to-ℓ alterations with normal crossings
items.statement: If X is separated and integral of finite type over a field L, ℓ is invertible in L, and Y ⊂ X is a proper closed subscheme, there are a finite extension L′/L of degree prime to ℓ, a connected smooth quasi-projective variety X′ over L′ and a proper surjective L-morphism π : X′ → X with L′(X′)/L(X) finite of degree prime to ℓ, such that π^{−1}(Y)_red is a strict normal crossings divisor on X′.
items.note: PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23 proposes the Part II PrimeToDegreeAlterations for exactly this degree control (its odd-degree case).

items.name: Theorem 2.13: strong density and finite-presentation injectivity
items.statement: Let K/k satisfy (SD): every k-variety with a K-point has a k-point. Let F be a contravariant set-valued functor on k-schemes satisfying (FP), compatibility with filtered colimits of k-algebras. For every geometrically integral k-variety V, F(k(V))→F(K(V)) is injective. For set-valued F prove this by starting with two elements having equal images, not by saying an element vanishes.
items.note: A general statement about étale cohomology and limits, with Greenberg's strong-density theorem as input.

items.name: Gysin sequences for ℓ-coefficients
items.statement: For a closed immersion i : Y ↪ X of smooth varieties of pure codimension c and n invertible: H^{ν−1}(U, Z/n(r)) →δ H^{ν−2c}(Y, Z/n(r−c)) →i_* H^ν(X, Z/n(r)) → H^ν(U, Z/n(r)) → ⋯ with transitivity for Y′ ⊂ Y ⊂ X, via purity H^{ν−2c}(Y) ≅ H^ν_Y(X).
items.note: EDC.3 plans purity i^!Λ ≅ Λ(−c)[−2c] and Gysin maps with transitivity.

items.name: Gysin morphisms, purity and weak Lefschetz for logarithmic de Rham–Witt cohomology
items.statement: Over a perfect field of characteristic p, with n = p^m: Gysin morphisms i_* for W_mΩ_log-cohomology with transitivity (Gros); for X smooth of pure dimension d, canonical Gysin isomorphisms H^{ν−2c}(Y, Z/p^m(d−c)) ≅ H^ν_Y(X, Z/p^m(d)) (Suwa, Cor. 2.6), hence the Gysin sequence in twist r = d; and weak Lefschetz H^{d+1}(Ū, Z/p(d)) = 0 for affine U of dimension d (Suwa, Lemma 2.1).
items.locator: §3, p. 27, and proof of Theorem 3.1, p. 28
items.note: The p-part input of Theorem 3.1: purity and Gersten theory for logarithmic Hodge–Witt sheaves on smooth varieties, a de Rham–Witt statement (RS-28 keeps only higher-field coefficient interfaces in HL.2).

items.name: Weak Lefschetz / affine vanishing for ℓ-coefficients
items.statement: For an affine variety U of dimension d over a separably closed field and ℓ invertible, H^{d+1}(U, Z/ℓ) = 0, so H^d(U, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(j)) is divisible.
items.note: EDC.4 uses imported affine Artin vanishing (its PR196/EtaleBaseChange Layer 6 supplier), not a second proof owner. The exact upstream source-to-declaration adapter remains part of G4; its rational/divisible coefficient consequences need their own limit argument.

items.name: Theorem 3.1: the crucial exact sequence
items.statement: Let K be finitely generated, X smooth proper irreducible of dimension d over K, and Y = Y_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ Y_r (r ≥ 1) smooth divisors meeting transversally with X ∖ Y_1 affine; U = X ∖ Y. For every prime ℓ (G_K = Gal(K̄/K^per)), the sequence 0 → H^d(Ū, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(d))_{G_K} →e H⁰(Y̅^{[d]}, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ)_{G_K} →d_2 H²(Y̅^{[d−1]}, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(1))_{G_K} is exact, where e is the composite of Gysin residues (3.2) and d_2 = Σ_μ (−1)^μ δ_μ with δ_μ the Gysin maps for Y_{i_1,…,i_d} ↪ Y_{i_1,…,î_μ,…,i_d}.
items.locator: Theorem 3.1, p. 27, proof pp. 28–31; statement and proof as corrected by E6
items.note: The components Y_i must be allowed reducible for the induction (E6). Remark 3.21: e and d_2 are, up to sign, the edge map and differential of the weight spectral sequence.

items.name: Definition 3.5: unramified cohomology
items.statement: For F a function field over k and n invertible in k, H^i_nr(F/k, Z/n(j)) ⊆ H^i(F, Z/n(j)) consists of the classes in the image of H^i_ét(Spec A, Z/n(j)) for every discrete valuation ring k ⊂ A ⊂ F.
items.note: Bloch–Ogus theory. PAPER-BENOIST-WITTENBERG-20 routes the coniveau/Cousin/Zariski-cohomology-sheaf package to SF.2.

items.name: Bloch–Ogus–Gabber: universal exactness of the Gersten resolution
items.statement: For a regular semilocal ring O essentially smooth over a field and Λ = Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ (ℓ ≠ char, or ℓ = char with twist d), the Gersten (Bloch–Ogus) sequence H^d(O ⊗_K M, Λ(d)) → H^d(K(X) ⊗_K M, Λ(d)) → ⊕_{x∈X¹} H^{d−1}(K(x) ⊗_K M, Λ(d−1)) is exact for finite Galois M/K and stays exact after taking Gal(M/K)-coinvariants ([CTHK97] Cor. 6.2.4, Ex. 7.3(1), 7.4(3)); hence the Zariski sheaf complex associated with C^{r,s}(Ū)_{G_K} is a flasque resolution of the coinvariant cohomology sheaf.
items.note: The effacement/Cousin package routed to SF.2 by PAPER-BENOIST-WITTENBERG-20.

items.name: Theorem 3.8: the Hasse principle for unramified cohomology
items.statement: Let K be a global field, n ∈ N invertible in K and F a function field in d > 0 variables over K with K separably closed in F. Then restriction induces an isomorphism H^{d+2}_nr(F/K, Z/nZ(d+1)) ≅ ⊕_v H^{d+2}_nr(F_(v)/K_(v), Z/nZ(d+1)).
items.locator: Theorem 3.8, p. 32, proof pp. 32–40; Case 3.8.B as corrected by E5
items.note: Injectivity by Theorem 2.10; surjectivity by Lemma 3.15 and Theorem 3.17 (Case 3.8.A) and an alteration argument (Case 3.8.B).

items.name: Lemma 3.15: the cokernel map as a map of coinvariants
items.statement: In the situation of Case 3.8.A, the map coker β(F/K) → ⊕_{x∈X¹} coker β(K(x)/K{x}) (3.14) identifies with H^d(FK̄, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(d))_{G_K} → (⊕_{y∈X̄¹} H^{d−1}(K̄(y), Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(d−1)))_{G_K} induced by the residue maps of X̄.
items.note: Via (3.16): coker(H²(K, M) → ⊕_v H²(K_v, M)) ≅ M(−1)_{G_K} functorially.

items.name: Theorem 3.17: injectivity on coinvariants of the Bloch–Ogus residue
items.statement: Let K be finitely generated with perfect hull L, X smooth proper irreducible of dimension d > 0 over K and ℓ a prime; assume ℓ invertible in K or RS2(U) for every open U ⊂ X ×_K L. Then (⊕_{y∈X̄⁰} H^d(K̄(y), Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(d)))_{G_K} → (⊕_{x∈X̄¹} H^{d−1}(K̄(x), Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(d−1)))_{G_K} is injective.
items.locator: Theorem 3.17, p. 35, Cases 3.17.A–C, pp. 35–38; statement as corrected by E4
items.note: Restore the positive-dimensional scope of the surrounding argument; E18 gives the d=0 counterexample to the isolated printed statement.

items.name: Remark 4.6: the case X = Spec L, and the reformulation of Conjecture 2
items.statement: (a) For X = Spec L, L/K finite, Conjecture 4.5 is the n-torsion of 0 → Br L → ⊕_w Br L_w →Σ inv_w Q/Z → 0. (b) Conjecture 4.5 follows from: (i) α_{X,n} is injective and (ii) H_0(C′(X, Z/nZ)) = Z/nZ, H_a(C′) = 0 for a > 0; conversely, by (a) and induction on dimension, when the function fields occurring have smooth proper models over K^per.

items.name: Theorem 4.8(a): injectivity of α_{X,n}
items.statement: Let K be a global field, n invertible in K and X a connected smooth proper variety over K. Then α_{X,n} : C^{2,1}(X, Z/nZ) → ⊕_v C^{2,1}(X_v, Z/nZ) is well defined and injective.
items.note: Residue field by residue field from Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 0.4, then Proposition 4.10.

items.name: Theorem 4.8(b): homology of the cokernel C′(X)
items.statement: In Theorem 4.8, if K is a number field or resolution of singularities holds over K, then H_a(C′(X, Z/nZ)) = Z/nZ for a = 0 and 0 for a ≠ 0.
items.locator: Theorem 4.8, p. 44, (b); proof via (4.12), Lemmas 4.14–4.15 and Theorem 4.19

items.name: Proposition 4.10: Henselization to completion is injective on Kato complexes
items.statement: For every variety V over K_(v), n invertible in K and r, s ∈ Z, C^{r,s}(V, Z/nZ) → C^{r,s}(V ×_{K_(v)} K_v, Z/nZ) is injective.
items.note: From Theorem 2.12 applied residue field by residue field.

items.name: Theorem 4.11: rigidity for Kato complexes (Jannsen, arXiv:1503.08742)
items.statement: For every variety V over K_(v), n invertible in K and r, s ∈ Z, C^{r,s}(V, Z/nZ) → C^{r,s}(V ×_{K_(v)} K_v, Z/nZ) is a quasi-isomorphism.
items.note: Cited, not proved here. It lets one replace X_v by X_(v) (4.12).

items.name: Lemma 4.14: the cokernel complex as coinvariants of C^{0,0}
items.statement: For n invertible in K, the complex C̄(X, Z/nZ) = coker(β_{X,n} : C^{2,1}(X, Z/nZ) → ⊕_v C^{2,1}(X_(v), Z/nZ)) (4.13) is canonically C^{0,0}(X̄, Z/nZ)_{G_K}: ⋯ → ⊕_{x∈X_r} H^r(K(x) ⊗_K K̄, Z/nZ(r))_{G_K} → ⋯ → ⊕_{x∈X_0} H⁰(K(x) ⊗_K K̄, Z/nZ)_{G_K}.

items.name: Lemma 4.15: passing between Z/ℓ^m and Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ coefficients
items.statement: Let K be a global field, X connected smooth proper over K and ℓ a prime; β_{X,ℓ^∞} = colim_m β_{X,ℓ^m} with cokernel C̄(X, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ). (a) β_{X,ℓ^∞} is injective iff all β_{X,ℓ^m} are. (b) H_a(C̄(X, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ)) = 0 (a ≠ 0) and H_0 = Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ iff H_a(C̄(X, Z/ℓ^m)) = 0 (a ≠ 0) and H_0 = Z/ℓ^m for all m.
items.note: From BK and cohomological dimension; (4.16)–(4.17).

items.name: Definition 4.18: resolution of singularities (RS)_L
items.statement: For a perfect field L: (RS1)_L every integral proper L-variety has a proper birational morphism from a smooth L-variety; (RS2)_L every smooth affine L-variety U has an open immersion into a smooth projective X with X ∖ U a simple normal crossings divisor. (RS)_L means both. RS2(U) at the start of §2 is (RS2) for one U. By Hironaka, (RS)_L holds in characteristic 0.
items.note: The RS predicates are conditional in characteristic p. R09.7 supplies characteristic-zero embedded resolution and the quasi-projective compactification interface, but an arbitrary-proper RS1 adapter must not be inferred without proof. Route 9 is held for revision.

items.name: Theorem 4.19: Kato's conjecture for coinvariant complexes, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ coefficients
items.statement: Let K be finitely generated with algebraic closure K̄ and perfect hull K^per, ℓ a prime and X an irreducible smooth proper variety over K, and assume resolution of singularities holds over K^per. Then for C̄(X, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) := C^{0,0}(X̄, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ)_{G_K} (G_K = Gal(K̄/K^per)), H_0 = Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ and H_a = 0 for a ≠ 0.
items.note: Implies Theorem 0.11 and, with Lemma 4.20, Theorem 0.10. Proved as Theorem 5.12 plus Lemma 4.24.

items.name: Lemma 4.20: C^{1,0} over a finite field as coinvariants
items.statement: Let k be finite and X a variety over k. (a) C^{1,0}(X, Z/ℓ^nZ) ≅ C^{0,0}(X ×_k k̄, Z/ℓ^nZ)_{G_k}. (b) 0 → C^{1,0}(X, Z/ℓ^n) → C^{1,0}(X, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) →ℓ^n C^{1,0}(X, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) → 0 is exact.
items.note: H^{m+1}(F, Z/ℓ^n(m)) ≅ H^m(Fk̄, Z/ℓ^n(m))_{G_k}, and BK plus cohomological dimension.

items.name: Definition 4.22: a homology theory with localization
items.statement: A homology theory on a category 𝒞 of finite-type L-schemes closed under open and closed immersions is a family of functors H_a on 𝒞_* (proper maps) with contravariance j^* for open immersions and functorial long exact localization sequences ⋯ → H_a(Y) → H_a(X) → H_a(V) →δ H_{a−1}(Y) → ⋯; morphisms commute with these.
items.note: General formalism (Bloch–Ogus, Jannsen–Saito) that the weight-homology comparison needs.

items.name: Lemma 4.23 and Remark 4.25: Kato homology is a homology theory
items.statement: Let L be a field and r, s ∈ Z and n ≥ 1 with n invertible in L, or r ≠ s + 1, or p = char L | n, r = s + 1 and [L : L^p] ≤ p^s. (a) H^{r,s}_a(X, Z/nZ) := H_a(C^{r,s}(X, Z/nZ)) extends to a homology theory on all L-varieties, via the componentwise split exact sequences 0 → C(Y) → C(X) → C(U) → 0. (b) The same holds for H̄^{r,s}_a(X) := H_a(C^{r,s}(X̄, Z/nZ)_{G_L}). These satisfy condition 4.24(i): H_a(L(X)) = 0 for a ≠ dim X.

items.name: Definitions 5.1–5.3: weight homology and cohomology of a normal-crossings pair
items.statement: For X smooth proper of dimension d over k and Y = Y_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ Y_r a simple normal crossings divisor (ordered components), and an additive covariant functor F on smooth proper k-varieties, L^iF(X, Y) is the i-th homology of 0 → F(Y^{[d]}) → ⋯ → F(Y^{[1]}) → F(X) → 0 with ∂ = Σ_ν (−1)^ν δ_ν; dually R^iG(X, Y) for contravariant G. For an abelian group A, H_0(X, A) = A ⊗ Z[π_0(X)] and H⁰(X, A) = Map(π_0(X), A) give the weight homology H^W_i(X, Y; A) = H_i(C^W_·(X, Y; A)) and weight cohomology H^i_W(X, Y; A).
items.locator: Definition 5.1, p. 52, Remark 5.2 and Definition 5.3, pp. 52–53
items.note: Definition 5.3 calls H⁰(−, A) covariant; it is contravariant (Remark 5.2).

items.name: Corrected Proposition 5.4: vanishing after a stratum-meeting divisor
items.statement: Let X/k be smooth proper of pure dimension d≥1, with an ordered SNC divisor Y. Let D be a smooth divisor transverse to every boundary stratum, such that D meets each connected component of Y^[j] in a nonempty connected scheme for j≤d−2 and in a nonempty scheme for j=d−1. Set Z=Y∪D. For every abelian group A, H^W_i(X,Z;A)=0=H_W^i(X,Z;A) for i≤d−1. This is Proposition 5.4 with the missing nonemptiness condition restored; a sufficiently general ample hyperplane supplies it over an infinite field.
items.note: Two disjoint fibres in P¹×P¹ disprove the printed version. The later ample-hyperplane applications satisfy the added condition.

items.name: Proposition 5.7: Theorem 3.1 as a weight-homology statement
items.statement: For U = X ∖ Y as in §5 there are canonical maps e : H^d_ét(Ū, Z/nZ(d)) → H^W_d(X, Y; Z/nZ); if k is finitely generated and some X ∖ Y_ν is affine, they induce isomorphisms H^d_ét(Ū, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(d))_{G_k} ≅ H^W_d(X, Y; Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) for all primes ℓ.
items.note: The affine-complement hypothesis must be retained. The arbitrary-divisor wording of Proposition 5.4 does not supply it; a chosen ample hyperplane does.

items.name: Theorem 5.9: weight homology of all varieties
items.statement: Let k be a field with perfect hull L, A an abelian group, and assume (RS1)_L. There is a homology theory H^W_a(−, A) on all k-varieties with proper maps such that (i) H^W_a(X, A) = A for a = 0 and 0 otherwise, for X smooth proper connected; (ii) for X smooth proper and Y a simple normal crossings divisor, H^W_a(X ∖ Y, A) ≅ H^W_a(X, Y; A) = H_a(⊕_{π_0(Y^{[d]})} A → ⋯ → ⊕_{π_0(Y^{[1]})} A → ⊕_{π_0(X)} A). For general k, H^W_a(Z, A) := H^W_a(Z ×_k k^per, A).
items.note: By Gillet–Soulé's method: X ↦ ⊕_{π_0(X)} A = Hom(CH⁰(X), A) extends to Chow motives. The printed (ii) writes Y^{[e]} for Y^{[d]}.

items.name: Theorem 5.10: weight homology of function fields
items.statement: If resolution of singularities holds over the perfect hull of k, then H^W_*(−, A) satisfies 4.24(ii): for every integral Z of dimension d, H^W_a(k(Z), A) := colim_V H^W_a(V, A) = 0 for a ≠ d.
items.note: Via Proposition 5.4. For finite k, a norm argument over p-power and q-power extensions (Tr ∘ Res = degree).

items.name: Theorem 5.12: Kato homology equals weight homology
items.statement: Let ℓ be a prime and K a finitely generated field with (RS) over L = K^per. Let H̄_*(−, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) = H_*(C^{0,0}(−, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ)_{G_K}) (Lemma 4.23(b)) and H^W_*(−, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) (Theorem 5.9). There is a morphism of homology theories φ : H̄ → H^W satisfying (i)–(iii) of Lemma 4.24, so φ is an isomorphism; with 5.9(i) this gives Theorem 4.19.
items.locator: Theorem 5.12, p. 58, proof pp. 64–66 with Lemma 5.25; proof as completed by E7
items.note: The printed proof of 4.24(iii) says (RS2) holds 'because K has characteristic zero' and omits the finite-field Bertini step (E7).

items.name: Theorem 5.13: extension of homology of a complex-valued functor
items.statement: Let k be perfect with resolution of singularities, 𝒜 an abelian category, and C:SP_k→C_{≥0}(𝒜) a covariant functor on smooth proper varieties such that each X↦H_a(C(X)) extends to a contravariant functor on the source's effective Chow-motive category. Then the homology functors extend naturally to a homology theory on all k-varieties. Only H_a(C), not C itself, is assumed to factor through motives. Apply C to chosen actual hyperenvelopes and their cone bicomplexes; establish independence through the spectral sequence and the motivic factorization on its E₂ page.
items.note: E16 corrects the unsupported chain-level factorization claim. Detailed construction is a remaining proof-provider gap, not an added hypothesis that C itself factors through motives.

items.name: Proposition 5.16: comparison with the naive homology theory
items.statement: Under the perfect-field/resolution setting of Theorem 5.13, let C:(V_k)_*→C_{≥0}(𝒜) be covariant for proper maps, with pullbacks for ALL open immersions and functorial short exact localization sequences 0→C(Y)→C(Z)→C(U)→0 for closed Y⊂Z, U=Z∖Y. Suppose the homology of C on smooth proper varieties factors through the specified effective Chow motives. Then the naive homology theory H_a(C(Z)) agrees canonically with the extension of C|SP from Theorem 5.13.
items.locator: Proposition 5.16, pp. 60–61; corrected E9 and E20
items.note: Following Gillet's descent theorem [Gil84] 4.1 and SGA 4 Vbis 3.3.3, with the corrected diagram of loc. cit. 3.3.3.3.

items.name: Gillet–Soulé: hyperenvelopes induce homotopy equivalences of Chow motives
items.statement: Under resolution of singularities, a proper variety has smooth proper hyperenvelopes, and a hyperenvelope g : W· → Z· of smooth proper simplicial varieties induces a homotopy equivalence g_* : M(W·) → M(Z·) of complexes of Chow motives; hence the weight complex M(V)· of a variety is well defined up to homotopy and representable by a finite complex.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.13, pp. 58–59 ([GS96] 1.4.1, Lemma 2, Proposition 2)
items.note: Use covariant motives throughout the proof; the opposite contravariant convention reverses all arrows together. Proper versus projective generators require the adapter in G8.

items.name: Effective Chow motives CHM^eff(k)
items.statement: The additive category of integral correspondences modulo rational equivalence on smooth PROJECTIVE varieties over k, followed by idempotent completion, gives effective Chow motives. Fix one variance convention. The full pure-motive category additionally inverts the Tate object; that localization is not part of the effective category.
items.note: MC.0–MC.1 plan this projective carrier. Jannsen's all-smooth-proper generator category and its comparison with the projective version are a separate unresolved adapter (G8); no rigid self-duality of effective motives is inferred.

items.name: Lemma 5.20: Chow correspondences act on Kato homology
items.statement: (a) For X smooth proper over k, H^{r,s}_a(X, Z/nZ) := H_a(C^{r,s}(X, Z/nZ)) extends to a contravariant functor on CHM^eff(k) if n is invertible in k, and also for k perfect of characteristic p, n = p^m and (r, s) = (0, 0). (b) The same holds for H_a(C^{r,s}(X̄, Z/nZ)_{G_L}). Proof: H^{r,s}_a(X) ≅ H^{d−a}(X_Zar, 𝓗^{r+d}_n(s+d)) (Bloch–Ogus; Gros–Suwa for p), with Barbieri-Viale's products, pullbacks and proper pushforwards on 𝓗-cohomology, H^e(Y × X, 𝓗^e_n(e)) ≅ CH^e(Y × X)/n, and Gillet's sign conventions.
items.note: Needed to apply Theorem 5.13 to Kato complexes. arXiv v2 used this hypothesis without checking it; the published version adds this lemma.

items.name: Lemma 5.25: the comparison diagram for U = X ∖ Y
items.statement: For U ⊂ X ⊃ Y as in (RS2) with X ∖ Y_1 affine, there is a commutative diagram with rows 0 → H^d(Ū, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(d))_{G_K} →e H⁰(Y̅^{[d]})_{G_K} →d_2 H²(Y̅^{[d−1]}, 1)_{G_K}, then 0 → H̄_d(U) → H̄_0(Y^{[d]}) → H̄_0(Y^{[d−1]}), then 0 → H^W_d(U) → H^W_0(Y^{[d]}) → H^W_0(Y^{[d−1]}), with vertical maps γ (Bloch–Ogus edge maps, and the trace H²(C, Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(1)) ≅ Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ on curves) and φ. Hence φ_U ∘ γ_U is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Lemma 5.25, p. 65, and the proof of Theorem 5.12, pp. 65–66

items.name: Poitou–Tate degree-two tail with discrete/compact dual conventions
items.statement: For a global field K, prime ℓ≠char K and discrete ℓ-primary torsion G_K-module N, the global-to-local degree-two sequence H²(K,N)→⊕_v H²(K_v,N)→H⁰(K,N*)^∨→0 is exact, where N*=Hom(N,μ_{ℓ∞}) has its compact topology, and real-place terms use the appropriate Tate conventions. Finite N is the finite-coefficient case; passage to arbitrary discrete N requires the compatible limits and duality, not reuse of a finite-module theorem without an adapter.
items.locator: Proofs of Proposition 1.2, Lemma 1.3 and Theorem 1.5, pp. 9–16
items.note: R02.4 owns the exact sequence and limit arguments. The additional archimedean surjectivity and high-degree assertions of the old bundle are isolated as missing proof interfaces in G3.

items.name: Hochschild–Serre spectral sequences for F/FK̄ and F_(v)/FK̄
items.statement: Let K be global, F/K a primary function field of transcendence degree d, ℓ≠char K, and M a discrete ℓ-primary torsion G_F-module. The exact Galois-group extension gives E₂^{p,q}=H^p(K,H^q(FK̄,M))⇒H^{p+q}(F,M), with compatible restriction maps for the Henselized local extensions. The bound used is cd_ℓ(FK̄)=d (and H^q=0 for q>d), not unqualified cohomological dimension at the residue characteristic.
items.note: R02.2 owns the continuous Hochschild–Serre construction. Field dimension and compatibility with residues/corestriction are separate inputs, retained in G3.

items.name: Theorem 1.5(b): the weight-nonzero lattice Hasse principle
items.statement: Let K be global and ℓ≠char K. If T is finite free over Z_ℓ with continuous G_K-action, and T⊗Q_ℓ is mixed with no weight zero, then for every finite set S′ of places, H¹_cont(K,T)→∏_{v∉S′}H¹_cont(K_v,T) is injective.

items.name: Theorem 2.5(a): permutation lattices satisfy (H)
items.statement: For K global, ℓ≠char K and I a finite-rank permutation G_K-lattice, C=I⊗Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(1) satisfies property (H) of item /23.

items.name: Theorem 2.5(b): stability across a permutation quotient
items.statement: For an exact sequence 0→I₁→I₂→I₃→0 of finite-rank discrete G_K-lattices with I₃ permutation, K global and ℓ≠char K, property (H) holds for I₁⊗Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(1) iff it holds for I₂⊗Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(1).
items.note: Restrict the weak-approximation argument to ℓ-primary exponents; E12 excludes all n in characteristic p.

items.name: Lemma 2.6: torus comparison for property (H)
items.statement: Let T/K be the torus with cocharacter lattice I, K global, ℓ≠char K, and C=I⊗Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(1). The surjectivity in (H)(i), respectively injectivity in (H)(ii), is equivalent to the corresponding map on the ℓ-primary parts of H¹(K,T), respectively H²(K,T), with the same local targets.
items.note: Tori, their lattice equivalence, Kummer sequences and permutation-torus/Shapiro adapters remain imported proof providers, not new definitions owned by this consequence.

items.name: Theorem 2.12: Henselization-to-completion injectivity
items.statement: For K global, F/K as in Theorem 2.10 and v a place, H^i(F_(v),Z/n(j))→H^i(F_v,Z/n(j)) is injective as stated for all n,i,j. The printed proof directly supplies fixed discrete étale coefficients; application to the characteristic-p logarithmic Hodge–Witt summand needs a separate (FP)/(SD) verification.
items.note: The prime-to-characteristic consequence is usable. The wild-provider gap G4 is explicit; no new source error is confirmed from the absence of its proof here.

items.name: Lemma 3.6: unramified classes as residue kernels
items.statement: For a function field F/k and n invertible in k, and each DVR A with k⊂A⊂F and fraction field F, the image of H^i_ét(Spec A,Z/n(j)) in H^i(F,Z/n(j)) is the kernel of its residue H^i(F,Z/n(j))→H^{i−1}(κ(A),Z/n(j−1)). Thus H^i_nr(F/k,Z/n(j)) is the intersection of these kernels.

items.name: Proposition 3.7: a smooth proper model computes unramified cohomology
items.statement: For X smooth proper integral over k, F=k(X) and n invertible in k, H^i_nr(F/k,Z/n(j)) is the kernel of the codimension-one residue sum on X and equals H⁰_Zar(X,𝓗^i_n(j)).

items.name: Lemma 4.24: the function-field comparison criterion
items.statement: Let L be perfect and 𝒞 a category of finite-type L-schemes closed under open and closed immersions. Let φ:H→H̃ be a morphism of homology theories. Suppose, for each integral Z of dimension d, the colimit groups H_a(L(Z)) and H̃_a(L(Z)) vanish for a≠d and φ_d is an isomorphism. Then φ is an isomorphism on every scheme of 𝒞.

items.name: The niveau spectral sequence of a homology theory
items.statement: For a homology theory with localization on finite-type L-schemes, the dimension filtration gives a natural strongly convergent sequence E¹_{p,q}(X)=⊕_{x∈X_p}H_{p+q}(κ(x))⇒H_{p+q}(X), where field groups are colimits over nonempty opens. Construct the filtration, connecting maps and finite-dimensional convergence; an abstract spectral-sequence carrier alone is not this construction.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 4.24, p. 52, citing Bloch–Ogus and Jannsen–Saito
items.note: Shared homological formalism: final unique owner and provider decomposition remain G7; route 9 is not accepted.

items.name: Corollary 5.5: top weight homology and change of coefficients
items.statement: Under the corrected Proposition 5.4 hypotheses (item /49), H^W_d(X,Z;Z) is finite free and H^W_d(X,Z;A)≅H^W_d(X,Z;Z)⊗A for every abelian group A. The analogous top weight-cohomology statement holds. Keep the universal-coefficient argument and freeness separate from any general duality claim.

items.name: Corollary 5.6: divisible top weight homology
items.statement: Under the corrected Proposition 5.4 hypotheses, H^W_d(X,Z;Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ) is divisible.

items.name: Remark 5.15: extending natural transformations
items.statement: If C and C′ satisfy Theorem 5.13 and φ:C→C′ is a natural transformation, then the hyperenvelope/cone construction induces a natural transformation of the extended homology theories.

items.name: Lemma 5.17: hyperenvelope descent for a localization complex
items.statement: For C under Proposition 5.16 and a hyperenvelope Z_•→X, the augmentation Tot C(Z_•)→C(X) is a quasi-isomorphism. Its proof must cover split Čech envelopes, noetherian-induction localization, and the coskeleton tower, including the convergence bound.
items.note: The source switches to C′ without defining a new functor; use C consistently. This is not generic étale hypercover descent.

items.name: The continuous-cohomology carrier
items.statement: For a topological representation A:TopRep k G, continuousCohomology n A is the n-th homology of TopRep.homogeneousCochains A, with values in TopModuleCat k.
items.note: Pinned declaration read. This supplies the carrier, not Poitou–Tate, Hochschild–Serre, cohomological dimension or geometric étale comparisons.

items.name: The nontrivial roots-of-unity Galois coefficient module
items.statement: For a field K, TauCeti.KummerCoeff K n is Additive(rootsOfUnity n (SeparableClosure K)), with its induced absolute Galois action and discrete topology.
items.locator: Coefficient (0.2), p. 2, twist one; TauCeti Coefficients.lean, lines 113–125
items.note: Pinned definition and continuous-action instance read. It does not provide all Tate twists or logarithmic Hodge–Witt coefficients.

items.name: The abstract spectral-sequence carrier

items.name: All-degree continuous restriction/corestriction and coefficient colimits
items.statement: For profinite G with discrete coefficients, continuous cohomology commutes with filtered coefficient colimits and carries all-degree restriction/corestriction for open subgroups, with cor∘res=[G:H] and naturality. Thus restriction to a finite extension of degree prime to ℓ is injective on ℓ-primary cohomology.

items.name: Coinvariant trace/restriction for an open subgroup
items.statement: For an open subgroup H of a profinite G and a discrete left G-module C, π:C_H→C_G is the natural quotient. The transfer τ:C_G→C_H sends [c] to Σ_{Ht∈H\G}[tc]. It is independent of representatives, and π∘τ=[G:H] on C_G; τ∘π is the norm, not generally multiplication by the index.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.10, p. 57; corrected E15
items.note: Finite-field component-module application produces Tr∘Res=degree; distinguish it from cohomological corestriction.

items.name: Finite-field continuous H¹ equals Frobenius coinvariants for torsion modules
items.statement: For k finite and M a discrete TORSION G_k-module, evaluation at arithmetic Frobenius induces H¹_cont(G_k,M)≅M/(Fr−1)M. Do not assert this for every discrete module: trivial Z is a counterexample.

items.name: Pythagoras number
items.statement: For a field F, p(F) is the least integer m such that every element expressible as a finite sum of squares is a sum of m squares; write infinity if no such m exists. State the zero/empty-sum convention, and use this definition for Corollary 0.7.
items.note: One owner with the existing QuadraticFormsRealFunctionFields candidate; not a new copy of the Witt ring.

items.name: Bertini hyperplanes with nonempty stratum intersections
items.statement: For a finite collection of smooth projective strata in a smooth projective variety over an infinite perfect field, choose a sufficiently general ample hyperplane transverse to all strata, avoiding the zero-dimensional strata, meeting each positive-dimensional connected stratum nontrivially, and with connected intersection on strata of dimension at least two. Over a finite field pass to finite extensions of prime-power degree and descend the vanishing statements through trace/restriction.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2, Proposition 5.4 and Theorem 5.10 proofs, pp. 18, 53, 56–57
items.note: The precise geometric connectedness and finite-extension descent interfaces need source-level decomposition (G9); do not infer nonemptiness from transversality.

items.name: Norm-residue consequence: finite-to-divisible coefficient injection
items.statement: For a field L, prime ℓ and t≥0, the norm-residue statement in degree t gives divisibility of H^t(L,Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(t)); the coefficient long exact sequence then makes H^{t+1}(L,Z/ℓ^m(t))→H^{t+1}(L,Q_ℓ/Z_ℓ(t)) injective, with image the ℓ^m-torsion. In characteristic ℓ this uses the logarithmic coefficient sequences, not an invertible-prime Kummer argument.

routes.title: Algebraic cycles, pure and mixed motives, Part II: weight complexes and weight homology
routes.brief:
First prerequisite: Algebraic cycles, pure and mixed motives (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles), especially MC.0 (correspondences) and MC.1 (Chow motives, with one fixed variance convention); do not replan them. The new object is weight homology: Gillet–Soulé's extension of functors on effective Chow motives to homology theories on all varieties via smooth proper hyperenvelopes and weight complexes (Gillet–Soulé, J. reine angew. Math. 478 (1996); Jannsen, Ann. of Math. 183 (2016), §§4.22–4.24 and 5).

The final theorems, as in Jannsen (published version):
- Theorem 5.9: under (RS1) over k^per, a homology theory H^W_*(−, A) on k-varieties with H^W_a(X, A) = A (a = 0), 0 (a ≠ 0) for X smooth proper connected, and H^W_a(X ∖ Y, A) ≅ H_a(⊕_{π_0(Y^{[d]})} A → ⋯ → ⊕_{π_0(X)} A) for simple normal crossings Y.
- Theorem 5.10: under (RS) over k^per, H^W_a(k(Z), A) = 0 for a ≠ dim Z, including the finite-field norm argument.
- Theorem 5.13 with Remark 5.15: extension of complex-valued functors C on smooth proper varieties, whose homology factors through CHM^eff(k), to homology theories; morphisms extend.
- Proposition 5.16 and Lemma 5.17: for a functor with open pullbacks and short exact localization sequences, the naive homology theory agrees with the extension (hyperenvelope descent after Gillet 1984 Theorem 4.1 and SGA 4 Vbis 3.3.3, with Jannsen's corrected diagram of 3.3.3.3).

Cover also: Definitions 5.1–5.3 (L^iF(X, Y), R^iG(X, Y), weight homology and cohomology of pairs; H⁰(−, A) is contravariant); Proposition 5.4 and Corollaries 5.5–5.6; the general homology-theory formalism of Definition 4.22 with localization sequences, the niveau spectral sequence and Lemma 4.24 (an isomorphism on function fields in the top degree, with vanishing elsewhere, gives an isomorphism of theories); Gillet–Soulé's hyperenvelope homotopy equivalence (GS96 Proposition 2) and the weight complex M(V)·. Use the corrected cross-references of sourceIssue E9 (Lemma 4.24 refers to Definition 4.22; Proposition 5.16 derives Ĥ via Theorem 5.13).

Hypotheses: characteristic 0 uses resolution from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.7. In positive characteristic (RS) is a named hypothesis, never a theorem. Do not add the removed arXiv §§6–7 as an optional branch of this published-paper route. Any alteration replacement of RS requires a separately checked Kerz–Saito or v2 extraction.

Import, never re-plan: Chow groups and proper pushforward (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5); correspondences and Chow motives (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.0–MC.1); smooth proper hypercovers and simplicial schemes (the hypercover formalism already used in AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5 and EnhancedDerivedSheaves E2); Bertini for hyperplane sections. Export H^W and Lemma 4.24 to HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheory HL.6, whose Theorem 5.12 compares Kato homology with weight homology.

Tests: a curve minus points (H^W_1 = Z^{#points−1}-type computation); P² minus a line and a transversal conic; a finite-field example needing the norm argument; independence of the choice of hyperenvelope and compactification.

Independent-review gate (not an accepted design brief): use corrected Proposition 5.4 with nonempty curve-stratum intersections (E10), preserve the affine-complement condition of Proposition 5.7, and use π∘Cor∨=degree (E15). Theorem 5.13 assumes only homology factors through motives, so do not apply C directly to abstract motives (E16). Separate the envelope definition, residue-field section condition, smooth proper hyperenvelope existence, compactification, refinement, totalization, coskeleton induction, boundedness and naturality. E2/L5 ordinary hypercover descent does not supply these motivic-envelope conclusions. MC.1's projective generators need an explicit all-smooth-proper comparison. Determine the owner of the general niveau/function-field criterion before creating a new homology-theory implementation. Route held for G7–G9.

review.notes: Full published-paper review. Clear corrections applied; unresolved atomic decomposition, proof-provider and ownership gaps explicitly recorded. Only individually accepted routes may be used.

gaps.title: Atomic extraction of the Kato core
gaps.detail: Separate each map, degree/twist convention, residue construction, square-zero, finite-support proof, local/global comparison, real-place case and finite/infinite coefficient implication. Lemma 1.3 alone has four conclusions. No single item may stand for the complete chain of imported proofs. HL.6 is the correct destination for the core, but the present route is held rather than represented as blueprint-ready.

gaps.title: Coefficient and finite-group algebra providers
gaps.detail: Separate all Tate twists and transition maps, the Brauer comparison, wild logarithmic exact sequences, equivalence of lattices with divisible cofinite torsion modules, Ext¹ base change for a finite group and the integral-lattice descent used on p. 20. Library /75–78 are partial carriers only. Do not infer an all-twist coefficient interface from μ_n alone. Existing Tau Ceti torus cocharacter finite-free/pairing APIs were found and opened; import these rather than planning a bare lattice again. Arithmetic weak-approximation APIs also exist; the prime-to-characteristic quotient/splitting-torus adapters are the missing comparison.

gaps.title: Global/local cohomological dimension and HS compatibility
gaps.detail: Supply actual field cd_ℓ bounds, high-degree localization at real places, H¹ archimedean and H² finite-set surjectivity, compact dual/limit conventions, and compatibility of Hochschild–Serre with residues and corestrictions. The field-constant components in Lemma 4.20 require the tensor-product/induced-module treatment. Do not assert cd_p equals transcendence degree of an arbitrary characteristic-p field.

gaps.title: Strong density and wild specialization
gaps.detail: Split (SD), (FP), Greenberg's theorem, étale filtered limits and Chevalley/open-image specialization. The source proof uses fixed discrete étale coefficients; verify the logarithmic Hodge–Witt functor's limit and specialization properties before claiming all n. This is an extraction closure gap, not a verified counterexample to Theorem 2.12. EDC.4 imports affine Artin vanishing from its PR196 supplier; record the exact provider rather than duplicate the proof.

gaps.title: Unramified and Gersten scope
gaps.detail: Read CTHK97 and the p-primary Gersten providers rather than conflate universal exactness with ordinary exactness. Distinguish all DVRs from divisorial valuations, and products of residue fields from a single geometrically integral component. Clarify the direct-sum/finite-support assertions in the arbitrary-valuation argument on pp. 39–40. No source mistake is confirmed for this unresolved scope question.

gaps.title: Geometric logarithmic purity and p-adic weights
gaps.detail: Independently source-check and split Gros Gysin maps/transitivity, Suwa purity at the exact twist, affine logarithmic vanishing, Milne/Katz–Messing weights and Gros–Suwa base change. CR.4, CR.5, RD.7 and HL.2 are distinct suppliers; choose one extension owner for the unowned scheme-level package, with explicit imports.

gaps.title: Homology formalism versus motivic descent ownership
gaps.detail: Settle one owner for general homology theories, niveau sequences and the function-field criterion. Decompose the GS96/Gillet/SGA4 proof of hyperenvelope descent and independence. Correcting E16's domain problem is not a full construction. E2 and L5 supply ordinary hypercover machinery, not automatic motivic-envelope descent.

gaps.title: Proper/projective motives and resolution adapters
gaps.detail: Jannsen switches between smooth projective and smooth proper generators. MC.0–MC.1 explicitly begin with projective varieties; R09.7d supplies quasi-projective compactification. Source-check the proper-to-projective correspondence adapter and KMP07 variance convention, as well as arbitrary-proper RS1. Do not manufacture rigid duals within effective motives.

gaps.title: Bertini, connected strata and finite-field descent
gaps.detail: Prove the nonempty/connected stratum Bertini interface and its exact base hypotheses, then finite-field prime-power extension and norm descent. Keep E10's corrected hypothesis and the independent affine-complement condition. Split the universal-coefficient and freeness arguments.

gaps.title: Primary versus geometrically integral function-field models
gaps.detail: In imperfect characteristic, K separably closed in F does not imply a geometrically integral smooth model over K; e.g. F=F_p(t^(1/p))(u) over F_p(t). Provide the purely inseparable constant-field reduction and compatibility maps before using such a model. This is an identified proof-provider gap, not an independently confirmed false main theorem.

gaps.title: Coinvariant Chow-correspondence action
gaps.detail: Check the primary BV97 and Gros–Suwa operations and the Galois-equivariant correspondence descent, including dimension/twist signs. An arbitrary cup product does not descend to coinvariants: for C₂ swapping the factors of Z×Z, [e₁]=[e₂] but [e₁²]≠[e₁e₂]. Correspondences defined over k can still act by equivariant operators; construct that action rather than assume a coinvariant ring.
